## Context / Problem

ADR 0056 already extracted `interpret_failure`, settings/usage builders, Agent kwargs, success logging, spend recording, and the provider session guard. ADR 0058 later removed per-file headroom assertions and made the locked 800-LOC module limit the only LOC ceiling. Current `origin/main` nevertheless has a 785-line `runner.py` and a 388-line `PydanticAIRunner.run()`.

This second pass must identify an ownership improvement in today's call graph. It must not repeat prior extraction, duplicate `ProviderSession` or `ExitStack`, introduce a generic hook/plugin bus, revive rejected frozen carriers without new evidence, or add a function-size ratchet.

## Approach

- Map the exact effect/resource timeline: event-loop displacement; config/preflight; tracing; provider/session construction; model/fallback scope; capability/cache/web settings; Agent execution; failure accounting; answer attribution; pre-finalization logging; finalization; run-shape/spend recording.
- Inventory semantic references plus string imports, monkeypatch targets, compatibility re-exports, globals mutated by alias, and tests that inspect source.
- Build a fault matrix for every raising boundary and identify the current owner of cleanup, accounting, provenance, and error translation.
- Compare candidate seams against `providers`, `model_classes`, `structured_run`, `agent_call`, `runner_support`, and ADRs 0056/0058. Prefer strengthening an existing owner.
- Record the ADR disposition before implementation. If the structure changes an accepted decision, complete the full ADR lifecycle.
- "No change is the right answer" is a licensed outcome of this research: if the census and fault matrix show the current decomposition already keeps every seam with a single, correct owner (ADR 0056 decision 4 argues `_check_tool_capability` and the fallback/capability sequencing must stay in `run()`'s body), the record states that conclusion and its evidence instead of manufacturing a marginal seam to satisfy this ticket.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/runner.py`, `agent_call.py`, `structured_run.py`, `providers.py`, `model_classes.py`, and `runner_support.py`.
- Runner/provider/cache/fallback/telemetry tests under `tests/unit/` and `tests/interfaces/`.
- `docs/adr/0056-*.md`, `docs/adr/0058-*.md`, and one new/amending ADR only if the research changes an accepted boundary.

## Testing

Build the fault matrix as executable characterization where possible. Happy path records the current effect/telemetry order. Each edge injects a raise at one boundary and observes resource closure, failure accounting, provenance, and downstream effects. Red-prove any proposed new guard against a deliberately broken local variant before treating it as useful.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The research record names every effect/resource boundary, its owner, its required ordering, and the observed behavior when it raises.
- [x] Semantic and text/string consumer censuses agree or every discrepancy is explained; monkeypatch and compatibility hazards are assigned to the change that moves/removes them.
- [x] A red-capable fault matrix covers raises before/after provider creation, fallback entry, external execution, finalization, and telemetry/accounting.
- [x] The selected design states exactly which existing module/class/function gains responsibility and which code is deleted; it does not create a second session owner or generic lifecycle framework.
- [x] Mutable provenance/settings and post-call answer attribution are modeled as the call graph actually treats them: the record states, for each, whether it is constructed once and read-only thereafter or mutated after construction, and any proposed seam keeps a mutated value mutable (no decorative frozen/immutable carrier wrapped around a value the call graph still mutates post-construction).
- [x] No function-NLOC ratchet, per-file headroom assertion, or new hard size threshold is proposed. Size measurements may be reported as advisory debt signals only.
- [x] The research critique identifies unanswered assumptions and conflicts; any necessary ADR amendment is explicitly approved/merged before implementation, or the record explains why ADR 0056 already authorizes the seam.
- [x] This ticket states explicitly, before close, which of two outcomes applies: (a) research-only — the record concludes no restructuring is warranted (or the identified improvement is deferred to a named, `discovered_from`-linked follow-on ticket), and this ticket closes on the research record and any characterization tests added under Testing above, with no further production change required; or (b) implemented — a selected seam is actually applied to the Scope's source files and `pytest tests/unit tests/interfaces` (scoped at least to the llm/runner/provider/telemetry suites) is green before close. The record names which outcome occurred and why.
